rationale: Large US cable brand with local sports ties; F1 interest would mainly be consumer marketing and US race hospitality.
changed: Renamed from Altice USA to Optimum Communications in 2025

name: Princeton Digital Group
desc: Singapore-based data centre developer and operator with campuses in Singapore, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia and Thailand.
markets: Data centres in Singapore, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia and Thailand serving cloud and internet customers.
rationale: Asian data centre operator that could use the Singapore Grand Prix for hospitality with cloud and AI customers.

name: Prysmian Group
desc: World's largest cable maker, producing power transmission, submarine, building and telecom cables and optical fibre.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific, serving utilities and telecom operators.
rationale: Global industrial brand with an Italian base and energy-transition message; B2B hospitality and technology tie-ins are plausible.

name: SBA Communications
desc: Owns and operates wireless towers in the US and Latin America leased to carriers such as AT&T.
markets: About 40,000 sites in the United States and Latin America leased to carriers.
rationale: Tower landlord selling to carriers rather than consumers; hospitality for carrier clients is the only real F1 angle.

name: Singtel
desc: Singapore's largest telecom operator, selling mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise ICT services domestically and through regional associates.
markets: Singapore, Australia through Optus, and stakes in mobile operators across Asia and Africa.
rationale: Brand-led telecom with Singapore Grand Prix home advantage and enterprise customers in Asia and Australia; strong hospitality and technology fit.

name: VodafoneZiggo
desc: Dutch telecom operator providing mobile, broadband, television and business services, a joint venture of Vodafone and Liberty Global.
markets: Customers in the Netherlands only; no international operations or verified expansion plans.
rationale: Large Dutch consumer brand with sports and event ties; Dutch F1 fan base supports marketing, though its focus is domestic.
changed: Formed in 2016 as a joint venture of Vodafone and Liberty Global

name: Zayo
desc: Fibre network and bandwidth provider operating long-haul and metro fibre across North America and Europe.
markets: Wholesale and enterprise fibre customers in North America and Europe.
rationale: Business-to-business bandwidth supplier to carriers and cloud customers; F1 could support hospitality and showcase network capacity for data-heavy events.
changed: Taken private by DigitalBridge and EQT in 2020

name: NBN Co
desc: Australian government-owned company that built and operates the National Broadband Network, selling wholesale broadband infrastructure to retail providers.
markets: Wholesale broadband across Australia only; no international operations.
rationale: Government-owned wholesale network with no retail brand; weak F1 fit despite the Australian Grand Prix.

name: Telecom Italia
desc: Italy's former state telephone monopoly, operating fixed and mobile telecom and ICT services for consumers and businesses as TIM.
markets: Consumers and businesses in Italy, plus mobile operations in Brazil through TIM Brasil.
rationale: Large Italian consumer brand with a Brazilian arm, both F1-relevant markets; sponsorship would suit brand marketing and hospitality.
changed: Sold its fixed network to KKR-led FiberCop in 2024

name: True Corporation
desc: Thai telecom and digital group offering mobile, broadband and digital services under the True and dtac brands.
markets: Customers in Thailand only; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Thailand's large consumer telecom brand with a young Asian audience; F1 hospitality and fan marketing are plausible but domestic.
changed: True and DTAC merged in 2023

name: Liberty Latin America
desc: Telecommunications company operating mobile, broadband and TV services in Puerto Rico, the Caribbean, Costa Rica and other Latin American markets.
markets: Consumers and businesses in Puerto Rico, the Caribbean and Central and South America.
rationale: Latin American consumer telecom brands could use F1 for marketing and hospitality in Mexico and Brazil, though budgets are limited.

name: Saudi Telecom Company
desc: Saudi Arabia's largest telecom operator, offering mobile, fixed broadband, enterprise and digital services including stc pay and towers.
markets: Saudi Arabia, plus operations in Kuwait and Bahrain and digital and tower businesses across the Gulf.
rationale: Already an F1 partner, with the Saudi Grand Prix in its home market; strong brand, hospitality and technology tie-ins.
f1: STC (stc) is a current F1 partner

name: Sunrise
desc: Swiss telecom provider and the country's second-largest operator, offering mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise services.
markets: Customers in Switzerland only; no international operations or verified expansion plans.
rationale: Large Swiss consumer brand with sports and entertainment sponsorship experience; F1 hospitality is plausible but market is domestic.
changed: Spun off from Liberty Global and listed on SIX in 2024

name: TowerCo
desc: Canadian wireless tower infrastructure company that leases space on its towers to wireless carriers.
markets: Canada on the data given; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Tower landlord selling to carriers with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is unlikely.

name: Elisa
desc: Finland's largest telecom operator, selling mobile, fixed broadband, TV and IT services to consumers and businesses.
markets: Customers in Finland and Estonia, plus digital services sold abroad.
rationale: Finnish consumer brand with a motorsport-loving audience; sponsorship fit is plausible but domestic scale limits budgets.

name: Crown Castle
desc: US real estate investment trust owning about 40,000 cell towers, plus small cells and fibre, leased to wireless carriers.
markets: Tower and fibre sites in the United States only, leased to carriers.
rationale: Tower landlord selling to carriers with no consumer brand; hospitality for carrier customers is the only F1 angle.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to sell its fibre and small-cell business

name: Swisscom
desc: Switzerland's leading telecom company, offering mobile, broadband, TV and IT services and owning Italian operator Fastweb.
markets: Switzerland, plus Italy through Fastweb; enterprise services across Europe.
rationale: Brand-led Swiss telecom with Italian operations and enterprise customers; hospitality and technology tie-ins are plausible but not obvious.

name: Telekom Srbija
desc: Serbia's state-controlled telecom group operating mobile (mts), fixed broadband, cable and IPTV services across Serbia and neighbouring countries.
markets: Serbia, plus mobile and cable operations in Bosnia and Montenegro.
rationale: State telecom with a strong Serbian consumer brand; budgets are modest and F1 relevance is limited.

name: Cable & Wireless Communications
desc: Former Caribbean and Latin American telecom operator offering mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise services under the Flow and C&W brands.
markets: Consumers and businesses across the Caribbean, Panama and other Latin American markets.
rationale: Now part of a larger group, so a sponsorship decision would sit with Liberty Latin America; F1 fit is limited.
changed: Acquired by Liberty Global in 2016; part of Liberty Latin America since 2017

name: Infrastrutture Wireless Italiane
desc: Italy's largest tower company, hosting mobile operators' equipment on more than 24,000 towers.
markets: Towers in Italy only, hosting Italian mobile operators.
rationale: Tower landlord selling to carriers with no consumer brand; Italian races offer only hospitality value.

name: Zain Saudi Arabia
desc: Saudi mobile operator, part of the Zain Group, serving consumers and businesses with mobile, broadband and digital services.
markets: Customers in Saudi Arabia only; group sister companies operate elsewhere in the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix host market where rival stc is already an F1 partner; strong brand, consumer and hospitality fit.

name: Axian Telecom
desc: Pan-African and Indian Ocean group running mobile operators, mobile money, fibre and data centres under brands such as Yas.
markets: Mobile operators in Madagascar, Tanzania, Senegal, Togo and other African and Indian Ocean markets.
rationale: Fast-growing African telecom and fintech group; Dubai base and Abu Dhabi or Miami hospitality could showcase brand, though budgets are modest.
